summary: Light set up in 1873 on the cape at the north-east entrance to Chaleur Bay; the 1939 concrete tower is still an active Coast Guard light, automated since 1987.

fog_signal.note: Fog alarm building added in 1913 with the quadruple-flash apparatus

structures.note: LighthouseFriends: 42 ft (12.8 m) to the vane. The heritage record gives about 5.4 m (18 ft). Unresolved.
The heritage record gives 14.6 m (48 ft); LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 46 ft (14 m)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). The keepers' houses are private rentals.

stay.note: The two former keepers' houses are rented as cottages (heritage record); LighthouseFriends describes a four-bedroom keeper's house rented by the week.

events.note: Station established 1873 (heritage record; Rowlett). LighthouseFriends: work began 1873; the light was first exhibited 1 September 1874.
Revolving gear broke; repaired by the Department's engineer, William Barbour (as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
A fire damaged the lantern room; new lamps and reflectors supplied
Quadruple-flash long-focus reflector installed; signature changed to four flashes every 25 seconds
The wooden tower was demolished and replaced by a concrete tower the same year
Tradition only, as LighthouseFriends states: part of Admiral Walker's fleet wrecked here on 11 August 1711. No record confirms it.

corrections.why: The heritage record says the two keepers' houses are rented as cottages, and LighthouseFriends describes a rented house. Nothing in the sources describes an inn.
LighthouseFriends gives 17 nautical miles for the present light; the station record gives 21. A human should check the Coast Guard list.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The heritage record and Rowlett date the station to 1873; LighthouseFriends says work began in 1873 and the light was first exhibited on 1 September 1874. The story reads 1873 as the station's establishment and 1874 as the first showing, which is LighthouseFriends' only evidence.

notes_for_editor: Read: RPCQ sector and tower records (French), Canadian Register 11182 (English), LighthouseFriends, Rowlett, and two Marine annual reports in the corpus. Not read: the DFHD federal heritage page 3100 (only a script shell came back). Wikipedia FR was read for leads only and is not cited (it says automated 1987 and designated 1988; the 1988 date is not confirmed by any source read, so it is left out). Conflicts left open: (1) first tower height 5.4 m (RPCQ) vs 42 ft (LighthouseFriends); (2) light range 17 nm (LighthouseFriends) vs 21 nm (station record); (3) the 1913 signature was 25 s (LighthouseFriends) and it is now 30 s in every source read; no source explains the change; (4) local unit: the station record says Le Rocher-Percé, the RPCQ sector record says municipality Gaspé in the MRC La Côte-de-Gaspé; the story says 'near Percé' to avoid choosing. Keepers: only Charles Bourget is checked against a Marine list (FY ended 31 March 1908, scan p. 192). That list is a multi-column table; the pairing 'Cape Despair Charles Bourget' is on one OCR line, but the page image was checked on 2026-10-27 (printed p. 183, scan 192): 'Cape Despair' and 'Charles Bourget' sit on the same row, with an appointment date of 1 November 1897 and a salary of $400; the row alignment is confirmed. The keepers Beck and Bourget dates after 1897 and the 1936 J. E. A. Beck entry come from LighthouseFriends only. The Marine statements for 1900 to 1924 in the corpus do not clearly assign the 1913 to 1914 works (quadruple flash, fog-alarm building, purchase of site) to this station, so they are not cited. Keeper's houses are rented; the family who bought them is named in Rowlett and LighthouseFriends, and is not named here because they are private persons. Two LighthouseFriends quotations are copyrighted; only short phrases are quoted, the rest is paraphrased. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the station record's Coast Guard entry gives a 21 nautical mile range and an 11.3 m structure height; the story attributes the 17 nautical mile range to LighthouseFriends and does not repeat the record's figures. The story has six chapters against the Moderate range of two to four; the editor should decide whether to merge chapters or treat the evidence as Rich (the body is about 1,000 words, Moderate by length).
